import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t = np.linspace(0, 1, 500)  # uniform time points from 0 to 1 second
x1 = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 1.0 * t)  # a 1 Hz reference signal

clips.caption: First prepare the <emphasis level="strong">time axis</emphasis> and a 1 Hz reference <emphasis level="strong">signal</emphasis>.

actions.text: x_task = 0.6 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 1.0 * (t - 0.2))  # shrink the amplitude to 0.6 and shift right by 0.2 s

clips.caption: Scale the <emphasis level="strong">amplitude</emphasis> by 0.6 and move the whole waveform 0.2 s to the right with t-0.2.

actions.text:
plt.figure(figsize=(7, 3))
plt.plot(t, x1, label="x1")
plt.plot(t, x_task, label="0.6 * x1 shifted right by 0.2 s")
plt.title("Scale and time shift")
plt.xlabel("Time (s)")
plt.ylabel("Amplitude")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

clips.caption: Draw the original and the transformed <emphasis level="strong">signal</emphasis> together and check that both <emphasis level="strong">amplitude</emphasis> and position match.

One way to write it is 0.6 times sin(2π times 1 times (t minus 0.2)). Observe: the <emphasis level="strong">amplitude</emphasis> is 0.6, the waveform moves right, and the <emphasis level="strong">period</emphasis> is still one second.
